chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

The post-childbirth woman (Nufasaa) refrains from prayer during the days of her regular period which she used to observe, then she performs ghusl and acts just as the one with irregular bleeding (Mustahaadha) does.

key_terms.أَقْرَائِهَا: Her regular periods (plural of Qar'), referring to the days she is accustomed to menstruating
key_terms.النُّفَسَاءُ: Post-childbirth woman (one who has just given birth)

ai.seo_question: How does a post-childbirth woman determine when to resume prayer and what ritual purity steps to follow?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of post-childbirth bleeding (Nufasaa) by establishing a hybrid ruling: the woman suspends prayer only for the duration of her habitual menstrual period, after which she performs ghusl and adopts the status of a mustahaaza (one with irregular bleeding). This distinction is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it differentiates Nufasaa from regular Hayd, allowing for a more lenient return to prayer while maintaining ritual purity through the specific rules of Istihaaza.
